messages.subject: Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() with no explanation
parts:
Running a model in INLA. 

This is on an server with 48 cores and 192GB of RAM, so doubt it is running out of memory.

Running the model in verbose mode, I see the regular "max.logdens= ....." lines output, then Eigenvalues, etc.  There are no warnings or errors, INLA seems happy.

Then, I get a series of output regarding  "config  0/157=[....]"

Then a crash
......
        config 127/157=[ -0.304 1.100 -0.445 1.281 1.424 -1.605 2.029 0.960 -1.676] log(rel.dens)=-2.955, [19] accept, compute, 23.22s
Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :


How can I diagnose the problem?  I tend to get this kind of crash around every 10 models I run, so understanding how to diagnose and fix the issue would be very helpful.

Thanks!!

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() with no explanation
parts:
Same as I use. The memory required is

A + #cores * B

so 192 is 4 pr core. can you try to reduce the number of cores used?

you might want to consider running the pardiso version, see

inla.pardiso()


and even the one compiled with MKL libraries,

inla.setOption(mkl=TRUE)

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() with no explanation
parts:
I also re-ran the model, watching memory use in another window.

You are correct.  Once INLA starts the "config" portion of output, the RAM quickly hits the system max, and starts swapping.  So, that is most likely the cause of the crash.

Thanks!

maximum should help,
